Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Qilu Enterprise, via its distributor Utopia Foods Inc. of Glendale, NY, recalled all lots of its 7.05-ounce (200-gram) packages of enoki mushrooms due to potential contamination with *Listeria monocytogenes*. The recall was initiated after routine sampling by the West Virginia Department of Agriculture found the presence of the bacteria. The New York State Agriculture Commissioner, Richard A. Ball, issued a consumer alert regarding the mushrooms which were distributed to wholesalers in New York, New Jersey, Pennsylvania, Massachusetts, and Maryland, and may have been sold in retail stores. The affected packages have the UPC code 928918-610109. Consumers who purchased the product were advised to return it to the place of purchase for a refund. At the time of the recall, no illnesses had been reported in connection with this specific product. <2> Eagle Produce LLC of Scottsdale, Arizona, voluntarily recalled 6,456 cases of whole cantaloupes in September 2023 due to potential Salmonella contamination. [1, 5, 6] The contamination was discovered following a test conducted on cantaloupes at a distribution center by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA). [1, 5, 6, 8] The recalled cantaloupes were distributed between September 5th and 16th, 2023, to numerous states, including California, Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kentucky, Louisiana, Maryland, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, North Carolina, North Dakota, Ohio, South Dakota, Tennessee, Texas, Virginia, West Virginia, Wisconsin, and Washington D.C. [1, 6] The recalled products were identified as Kandy Produce whole cantaloupes with the UPC number 4050 and lot codes 797901, 797900, and 804918. [5] At the time of the recall announcement, there were no reported illnesses associated with the consumption of the product. [6] The FDA conducted the testing that led to the recall. [1] <3> Twin City Foods, Inc. of Stanwood, Washington, initiated a voluntary recall for a limited quantity of its Not-Ready-To-Eat Individually Quick Frozen (IQF) Super Sweet Cut Corn and Mixed Vegetables due to potential contamination with Listeria monocytogenes. The recall was prompted by the results from a customer's third-party lab test on the IQF sweet cut corn. Among the affected products was the 16-ounce bag of Food Lion brand Super Sweet Cut Yellow Corn. Other brands involved in the recall included Kroger and Signature. <4> On August 10, 2023, Nestlé USA announced a voluntary recall of a limited quantity of its NESTLÉ® TOLL HOUSE® Chocolate Chip Cookie Dough "break and bake" Bar products. [1] The recall was initiated due to the potential presence of wood fragments, following a small number of consumer complaints. [2] The action was taken out of an abundance of caution, and no illnesses or injuries have been reported. [1, 2] The recall is isolated to two specific batches (311457531K and 311557534K) of the 16.5 oz bar product, which were produced on April 24 and 25, 2023, and distributed to retailers across the United States. [1, 3] No other Nestlé Toll House products are affected by this recall. [2] Consumers who purchased the affected products were advised not to consume them and to return them to the place of purchase for a replacement or refund. [1] <5> On August 9, 2023, Real Kosher Ice Cream of Brooklyn, NY, initiated a recall of all its "Soft Serve on the Go" ice cream and sorbet cups due to potential contamination with *Listeria monocytogenes*. The recall was prompted after the Pennsylvania Department of Agriculture found the bacterium in a product sample taken from the home of an individual who became ill. At the time of the recall, two hospitalizations were reported, one in New York and one in Pennsylvania. The recall covered all products manufactured up to August 4, 2023, which were distributed to canteens, convenience stores, and grocery stores in 19 states and the District of Columbia. The company ceased production and distribution while the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) investigated the cause. <6> Trader Joe's, in conjunction with its supplier Winter Gardens Quality Foods Inc., recalled approximately 10,889 cases of its Unexpected Broccoli Cheddar Soup due to the potential presence of insects in the broccoli florets. [2, 3, 6] The recall affected 20-ounce containers (SKU# 68470) with 'Use By' dates ranging from July 18, 2023, to September 15, 2023. [1, 4, 5] The recalled soup was sold in Trader Joe's stores across seven states: California, Connecticut, Florida, Illinois, Pennsylvania, Texas, and Washington. [2, 3, 7] According to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA), the manufacturer initiated the recall on July 10, 2023, and Trader Joe's publicly announced the recall on July 27, 2023. [2, 4, 5] No illnesses were reported in connection with the consumption of the soup. [1, 5] Customers who purchased the product were advised to discard it or return it for a full refund. [1, 4] <7> Ziyad Brothers Importing of Cicero, Illinois, issued a recall for its 35.2 fluid ounce packages of Ziyad brand Jameed Soup Starter. The recall was initiated because the product contains milk, a major allergen, which was not explicitly declared on the label. An internal company review found that while the ingredient list mentioned 'lactic casein powder', it did not clarify that this ingredient is derived from milk. The product was distributed nationwide in the United States through retail stores and Amazon. The recall applies to all packages with the UPC code 0 74265 00597 1. No illnesses were reported in connection with this issue. A subsequent recall was triggered in Canada for the same reason. Consumers who purchased the product were advised to return it to the place of purchase for a full refund. <8> On June 30, 2023, the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) announced that Panamerican Foods, LLC of Kearny, N.J., recalled approximately 4,978 pounds of canned pork and beef bean stew. The recall was initiated because the products were imported from an establishment in Brazil that is not eligible to export meat products to the United States, meaning they were not presented for FSIS import inspection. The specific products recalled were 430g cans of "Anglo Feijoada Pronta para servir" and "Bordon Feijoada PRONTO PARA SERVIR", which bear the establishment number "76 S.I.F." on the can. These items were distributed to retail locations nationwide. The issue was discovered after a referral from the USDA’s Smuggling Interdiction and Trade Compliance Program led to the products being found for sale in a retail store. There have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions from consuming these products. <9> On June 30, 2023, House of Raeford's establishment in Nesmith, South Carolina, announced a recall for approximately 76,961 pounds of Foster Farms brand mini chicken corn dogs due to possible spoilage. The U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) clarified the recall was initiated after consumer complaints regarding the product having an off odor, appearance, and unpleasant taste. The recalled products are 1.83-lb. resealable bags of "FOSTER FARMS MINI CORN DOGS BITE-SIZED CHICKEN FRANKS DIPPED IN BATTER HONEY CRUNCHY FLAVOR" with lot codes 123114 and 223114, a "best if used by" date of 4/23/24, and the establishment number "P-9136" on the package. The items were produced on April 24, 2023, and distributed to retail locations nationwide. There have been no confirmed reports of adverse reactions from consuming the products. Consumers were advised to either throw the products away or return them to the place of purchase.

While the company's internal testing did not find Salmonella in the final product, it did indicate that one of the food's components may contain the bacteria. The affected lot was distributed nationwide between May 6, 2025, and May 16, 2025, through retailers such as Petco, Walmart, Chewy, Amazon, and Meijer. The affected items, which have "Use By" dates from April 22, 2025, to May 19, 2025, were distributed to corporate offices, medical facilities, and vending machines in Arizona, California, Nevada, and Washington. [3, 5, 6] The product was sold at the Walker's Wine Juice retail store in New York and distributed to a limited number of commercial wineries in twelve states: Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Maine, Michigan, Minnesota, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin. Prediction target period: from 2025-08-03 to 2025-10-19. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Chetak LLC Group recalled multiple lots of Deep brand frozen Sprouted Moong (Mung) and Sprouted Mat (Moth) products following an investigation by the FDA and CDC into a multistate outbreak of Salmonella Anatum infections linked to the items. The recall was initiated after routine FDA product sampling in May 2025 confirmed the presence of Salmonella. The products were distributed nationwide to retail stores and through mail orders. The FDA published the recall announcement on July 24, 2025, based on information current as of July 17, 2025. <2> Jewel Osco, owned by Albertsons Companies, voluntarily recalled a variety of ready-to-eat tuna salad products from its stores in Illinois, Indiana, and Iowa. [1, 3] The recall was initiated after a supplier, Reser's Fine Foods, alerted them that breadcrumbs used as an ingredient in the tuna salad were potentially contaminated with *Listeria monocytogenes*. [1, 3] The recall included items such as tuna salad sandwiches, croissants, snack trays, and deli-packaged tuna salad with "Sell Thru Dates" between July 16, 2025, and July 19, 2025. [2, 5, 6] This action was part of a broader recall by Reser's Fine Foods that also affected other Albertsons-owned stores in several other states. [2, 4] No illnesses were reported in connection with the consumption of these products. [1, 4] Consumers were advised to dispose of the products or return them for a full refund and to sanitize any surfaces that may have come into contact with the items. [1, 3] <3> On July 14, 2025, Danone U.S. announced a voluntary recall of all flavors and sizes of its YoCrunch® yogurt products sold in retail stores nationwide. The recall was initiated after consumer complaints regarding the presence of transparent plastic pieces, which can be between 7 and 25 mm in length and may have sharp edges, in the dome toppers containing toppings like granola, M&M's, and Oreo pieces. This contamination poses a potential choking hazard. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) is cooperating with the recall, which was officially initiated on July 11, 2025. The issue is isolated to the toppings; the yogurt itself is not affected. Consumers are advised not to consume the products and can contact the YoCrunch Consumer Care Line for refund information. <4> Rhode Island-based grocery wholesaler, United Natural Foods, Inc. (UNFI), voluntarily recalled 30 different kinds of produce after a mechanical malfunction at its Allentown, Pennsylvania, distribution center potentially contaminated the products with fluid from a reach truck, a type of warehouse forklift. The recall affects 213 cases of produce distributed to retailers in Maryland, New Jersey, New York, Pennsylvania, and Washington, D.C. The list of recalled items includes apples, lettuce, broccoli, carrots, kale, lemons, and watermelon, among others. A UNFI spokesperson stated that the malfunction occurred on June 4, 2025, and the company issued the voluntary recall on June 7, 2025, out of an abundance of caution, with no illnesses having been reported. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) announced the recall publicly and assigned it a Class II classification on July 10, 2025, indicating a remote probability of serious adverse health consequences. <5> Natureen International Inc. of Walnut, CA, issued a recall for 244 bags of its 2.5-ounce Wei-Chuan Dried Black Fungus Slice due to potential Salmonella contamination. [3] The recall was initiated after the California Department of Public Health detected the pathogen and notified the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. [2, 3] The affected products are marked with lot number XJ17 and an expiration date of EXP:20260417. [2, 4] The dried fungus was distributed via the Wei-Chuan Chicago Branch to retail stores and supermarkets across 11 Midwestern states: Illinois, Indiana, Iowa, Kansas, Kentucky, Michigan, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Ohio, and Wisconsin. [3] As of the recall announcement, no illnesses had been reported. [8] Consumers are advised to return the product to the place of purchase for a full refund. [2] <6> On July 2, 2025, the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) announced that Kraft Heinz Foods Company was recalling approximately 367,812 pounds of its Oscar Mayer fully cooked turkey bacon products. The voluntary recall was initiated after the company's own laboratory testing indicated potential contamination with Listeria monocytogenes. The affected products were produced at its Newberry, South Carolina, establishment between April 24, 2025, and June 11, 2025. The recall impacts various package sizes of "Oscar Mayer Turkey BACON ORIGINAL" which were distributed to retail locations nationwide, as well as exported to the British Virgin Islands and Hong Kong. While there have been no confirmed reports of illness due to consumption, consumers are urged to either discard the products or return them to the place of purchase. Listeria contamination can cause listeriosis, a serious infection, especially for older adults, pregnant individuals, and those with weakened immune systems.

The recall was officially announced by the FDA on August 14, 2025. The cheese, identified by lot number 615, was initially distributed to Cheese Plate Park Slope LLC in Brooklyn, NY. It was subsequently cut and sold to customers at two locations, Cheese Plate Brooklyn - Park Slope LLC and Cheese Plate Brooklyn: Carroll Gardens, between July 24, 2025, and August 13, 2025. The recall was initiated after a foreign manufacturer alerted Fromi USA to the potential contamination. Wegmans is offering a full refund for returned products and has used its Shoppers Club data to place automated calls to customers who may have purchased the items. <3> Dollar General Corporation recalled three lots of its eight-ounce Clover Valley® Instant Coffee due to the potential presence of glass fragments. [5, 6] As of early August 2025, no illnesses had been reported in connection with the recall. [1, 2, 4] This action was a follow-up to a recall by Reser's Fine Foods, which identified potential Listeria monocytogenes contamination in breadcrumbs used as an ingredient in their tuna salad. [1, 2] The expanded recall now includes products with "best by" dates from July 23, 2024, to July 29, 2025, in addition to the previously recalled dates of July 16, 2025, to July 19, 2025. The recall was initiated after routine FDA product sampling in May 2025 confirmed the presence of Salmonella. The products were distributed nationwide to retail stores and through mail orders. The FDA published the recall announcement on July 24, 2025, based on information current as of July 17, 2025.

The action was taken after the company received numerous consumer complaints, which included five reports of minor injuries. The recalled products were produced between July 30, 2024, and August 4, 2025, and are marked with the establishment number “P-6137B” inside the USDA mark of inspection or on the packaging. These items were shipped to retail and institutional locations nationwide, including the Department of Defense and USDA Commodity Foods donations, a broader distribution than just the initially mentioned select Walmart stores. <2> On September 5, 2025, the Middlefield Original Cheese Co-Op of Middlefield, Ohio, initiated a recall of several cheese varieties due to potential contamination with Listeria monocytogenes. The recall was announced after company testing discovered the bacteria in finished products and on the surfaces of cutting equipment. The affected products were sold under the 'Middlefield Original Cheese Co-Op' and 'Sunrise Creamery' brand names and were distributed between July 7, 2025, and August 14, 2025, in Ohio, Minnesota, Wisconsin, and Texas. The recall includes specific lots of Organic Gouda, Mozzarella/Provolone, colored Cheddar, Swiss, Pepper Jack, Monterey Jack, and Sunrise Creamery Dilly Pickle Monterey Jack cheese. As of the recall announcement, there have been no reported illnesses linked to the consumption of these products. <3> The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued a public advisory on August 19, 2025, concerning potential Cesium-137 contamination in frozen shrimp products processed by PT. Bahari Makmur Sejati, an Indonesian firm. The FDA advised consumers, retailers, and distributors not to eat, sell, or serve the affected products. Following this, several companies initiated voluntary recalls. On August 21, 2025, Southwind Foods, LLC recalled various brands of raw and cooked frozen shrimp. Beaver Street Fisheries, LLC followed on August 22, 2025, recalling Great Value Frozen Raw Shrimp sold in select Walmart stores. On August 29, 2025, AquaStar (USA) Corp. also recalled thousands of packages of cocktail shrimp. The recalled products had been distributed to retailers, distributors, and wholesalers across at least 34 states between June and September 2025. <4> Fromi USA of New York, NY, issued a recall for 12 cases of Brie Royal Faucon 1kg cheese due to potential contamination with Listeria monocytogenes. The recall was officially announced by the FDA on August 14, 2025. The cheese, identified by lot number 615, was initially distributed to Cheese Plate Park Slope LLC in Brooklyn, NY. It was subsequently cut and sold to customers at two locations, Cheese Plate Brooklyn - Park Slope LLC and Cheese Plate Brooklyn: Carroll Gardens, between July 24, 2025, and August 13, 2025. The recall was initiated after a foreign manufacturer alerted Fromi USA to the potential contamination. At the time of the announcement, no illnesses had been reported in the United States in connection with the product. The FDA later assigned this a Class I risk classification, indicating a reasonable probability of serious health consequences from consumption. Consumers who purchased the cheese were advised to return it to the place of purchase for a full refund. <5> Wegmans Food Markets, Inc. has recalled its Medium Camembert Soft Ripened Cheese and a variety of prepared products containing the cheese due to potential contamination with Listeria monocytogenes. The recall was initiated after Wegmans' supplier, Estancia Holdings of Cumming, Georgia, was notified by its French supplier that three shipments might be contaminated. The affected products were sold between July 1 and August 12, 2025, at all Wegmans stores in Connecticut, Delaware, Maryland, Massachusetts, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Virginia, and Washington, D.C. As of the announcement, no illnesses had been reported. Wegmans is offering a full refund for returned products and has used its Shoppers Club data to place automated calls to customers who may have purchased the items. <6> Dollar General Corporation recalled three lots of its eight-ounce Clover Valley® Instant Coffee due to the potential presence of glass fragments. The recall was initiated after a customer reported the issue to the company. The affected coffee, identified by UPC 876941004069 and lots L-5163, L-5164, and L-5165, was distributed to Dollar General stores in 47 states between July 9 and July 21, 2025. The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) posted the company's announcement of the recall, which advises consumers to discard the product and contact Dollar General for a full refund. At the time of the recall, no injuries or illnesses had been reported. <7> Navarro Pecan Holdings, LLC of Corsicana, Texas, voluntarily recalled approximately 32,670 pounds of various pecan products due to potential contamination with Salmonella. [2, 3] The recall encompasses several varieties including Fancy Small Pecan Pieces, Fancy Midget Pecan Pieces, and various types of pecan halves. [2] The recall, initiated by the company on July 10, 2025, was classified as a Class 1 by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA), which is the highest-risk category, indicating a reasonable probability of serious health consequences or death from exposure. [3, 4, 6] The FDA posted the recall in an Enforcement Report on August 1, 2025. [3, 4] The affected pecans were distributed to bakeries, commercial kitchens, and food factories in Texas, Minnesota, Oklahoma, Arkansas, and New Jersey, as well as internationally to the United Arab Emirates, the Netherlands, and Italy. [2, 5] Consumers are advised not to eat the products and to sanitize any surfaces that may have come into contact with them. [5, 6] As of early August 2025, no illnesses had been reported in connection with the recall. [2]

samples.scenario: Prediction target period: from 2025-11-23 to 2026-02-08. Recent related events (events are separated by numbered tags): <1> Face Rock Creamery LLC initiated a voluntary recall of 16 units of its 6-ounce Vampire Slayer Garlic Cheddar cheese due to potential contamination with Listeria monocytogenes. The affected products were sold exclusively at the Face Rock Flagship retail store in Bandon, Oregon. <2> On November 11, 2025, ByHeart Inc. recalled all batches of its Whole Nutrition Infant Formula due to potential Clostridium botulinum contamination. The voluntary recall followed an FDA and CDC investigation linking the formula to a nationwide multistate outbreak of infant botulism. The outbreak is part of a larger spike involving approximately 83 infant botulism cases since August, with dozens of cases directly linked to the formula across multiple states. The contamination was identified after laboratory analysis detected the bacteria in an open can of ByHeart formula consumed by an affected infant in California. <3> Blue Oven Bakery, Inc. of Cincinnati, Ohio, issued a voluntary recall for its English muffins due to the presence of an undeclared milk allergen. The recall was initiated by the company on October 31, 2025, with the FDA publishing the public announcement on November 6, 2025. The affected product was sold fresh in a 13.04 oz sealed plastic bag at various markets in Ohio, Kentucky, and Indiana. The recall applies to all English muffins produced between April 24, 2025, and October 24, 2025. No illnesses or allergic reactions have been reported in connection with this recall. <4> Brazilian Taste, based in Lexington, South Carolina, recalled approximately 4,120 pounds of frozen chicken and beef croquette products. The recall was initiated due to misbranding and the presence of undeclared sesame, a known major food allergen, which was not listed on the product labels. <5> On October 29, 2025, Moonlight Companies voluntarily recalled California-grown conventional yellow and white peaches due to potential contamination with Listeria monocytogenes. The recall was initiated after the organism was found in the packing facility environment. The peaches were sold nationwide between September 16, 2025, and October 29, 2025, at numerous major retailers, including Sam's Club, Walmart, Costco, Kroger, Target, Trader Joe's, and Food Lion. The recalled fruit was sold individually with PLU stickers or in various multi-packs; products labeled "Washington" or "Organic" are not affected by this recall. At the time of the announcement, no illnesses had been reported. <6> On October 27, 2025, Homeneeds Inc. of Bellevue, WA, initiated a recall of its Devi brand Cinnamon Powder (Dalchini Powder). The recall was prompted by potential lead contamination after the FDA detected elevated levels of the substance in product samples. The affected product was packaged in 100-gram (3.5 oz) clear plastic bags. <7> Hormel Foods Sales, LLC, based in Austin, Minnesota, announced a voluntary recall of approximately 4,874,815 pounds (215,258 cases) of its HORMEL® FIRE BRAISED™ ready-to-eat frozen chicken products. The recall was initiated after several foodservice customers reported finding pieces of metal in the chicken breast and thigh products. Hormel determined the contamination was from a conveyor belt used in the production process. The affected items were distributed nationwide to foodservice operators, such as hotels, restaurants, and institutions, and were not sold directly to consumers. The recall, conducted with the knowledge of the USDA's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS), is classified as Class I. As of the announcement, no illnesses or injuries have been reported in connection with this recall. <8> On October 4, 2025, Foster Poultry Farms, LLC of Livingston, California, recalled approximately 3.9 million pounds of chicken corn dog and ground turkey on a stick products. The recall was due to potential contamination with extraneous material, specifically pieces of wood embedded in the batter. The action was taken after the company received numerous consumer complaints, which included five reports of minor injuries. The recalled products were produced between July 30, 2024, and August 4, 2025, and are marked with the establishment number “P-6137B” inside the USDA mark of inspection or on the packaging. These items were shipped to retail and institutional locations nationwide, including the Department of Defense and USDA Commodity Foods donations, a broader distribution than just the initially mentioned select Walmart stores. <9> A multistate outbreak of Listeria monocytogenes infections has been linked to prepared pasta meals, prompting a public health alert from the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS) and numerous recalls. The outbreak investigation involves the FSIS, the CDC, and the FDA. As of September 25, 2025, 20 illnesses, 19 hospitalizations, and 4 deaths were reported across 15 states. Subsequent reports by early November 2025 increased the numbers to 27 illnesses in 18 states, with 25 hospitalizations and 6 deaths. The investigation identified Nate's Fine Foods, Inc. as the supplier of the contaminated pasta, leading to expanded recalls in September. Recalled products were sold at various retailers including Walmart, Trader Joe's, Albertsons, Kroger, and others. Listeria infection is especially dangerous for pregnant women, newborns, older adults, and individuals with weakened immune systems, with symptoms such as fever, muscle aches, and confusion. The incubation period can range from a few days to several weeks after consuming contaminated food.
